questions.question: A sales team cannot send email because the mail service is down, and an agent picks up their incident. What is the agent's main objective under Incident Management?

options.text: Find the underlying root cause of the recurring outage
Restore normal service while minimizing business impact
Plan and approve a controlled change to the mail servers
Log the issue as a catalog request for later fulfillment

explanation.correct: ServiceNow describes Incident Management as restoring normal service operation while minimizing the impact on business operations and maintaining quality. The agent's job on this incident is to get the sales team sending email again as quickly as possible. Root cause analysis, change control and request fulfillment are each handled by separate ITSM processes. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/incident-management/c_IncidentManagement.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Identifying the cause of errors behind related incidents is the purpose of Problem Management. The incident itself focuses on restoring the service.
Controlling the life cycle of changes with minimum disruption is the role of Change Management, not the objective of working an incident.
Request Management handles requests for services, products or information. A service outage is an incident, not a catalog request to be fulfilled.

source.excerpt: The goal of incident management is to restore normal service operation as quickly as possible.

questions.question: A service desk agent tries to raise an incident's Priority directly on the form, but the field is read-only. By default, how is the Priority value set?

options.text: Agent sets Impact and Urgency, and lookup rules derive it
The caller picks a Priority when submitting from the portal
The assignment group manager sets it when accepting the work
It is copied from the Priority of the related problem record

explanation.correct: By default the Priority field is read-only and must be set by selecting the Impact and Urgency values. Priority lookup rules, configured by administrators, determine how impact and urgency combine into the priority of each incident. Priority then identifies how quickly the service desk should address the task. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/incident-management/def-prio-lookup-rules.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Nobody picks Priority directly by default, including the caller. The field is read-only and is derived from the Impact and Urgency values through the priority lookup rules.
Assignment group managers do not set Priority. It is derived from Impact and Urgency, and individual incident responders cannot change the priority lookup rules (only data_lookup_admin or admin can).
Priority is not inherited from a problem record. The Incident form's Priority field is based on the incident's own Impact and Urgency values.

source.excerpt: Priority is calculated using a lookup matrix based on Impact and Urgency.

questions.question: An agent has placed an incident On Hold with the On hold reason Awaiting Caller. The next day, the caller updates the incident with the requested details. What happens to the incident?

options.text: It stays On Hold until the agent manually changes the state
The On hold reason is cleared and the state moves to In Progress
It returns to the New state so the service desk can triage it again
It is resolved automatically with a No response from caller code

explanation.correct: In the incident life cycle, On Hold means responsibility has temporarily shifted to someone else, such as the caller, to provide information. When the caller updates an incident that is on hold, the platform clears the On hold reason and sets the state back to In Progress, the state for an incident that is assigned and being investigated. The assigned agent and the watch list are notified so work can resume. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/incident-management/c_IncidentManagementStateModel.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The incident does not wait for the agent: when the caller updates it, the platform clears the On hold reason and changes the state to In Progress on its own.
New is for an incident that is logged but not yet investigated. A caller update to an on-hold incident sends it to In Progress, not back to New for triage.
The No response from caller resolution happens when the caller does not respond after all reminder attempts. Here the caller did respond, so the incident resumes.

source.excerpt: The In Progress state indicates work has begun on the incident.

questions.question: An agent applies a fix and sets an incident to Resolved. A team lead asks why the incident has not moved to Closed yet. Which statement explains the difference between the two states?

options.text: Resolved and Closed are two names for the same final state
Resolved means a fix is in place; Closed follows confirmation
Resolved incidents are locked, but Closed ones can be reopened
Closed is an interim state that an incident passes before Resolved

explanation.correct: An incident is Resolved when a satisfactory fix has been provided. It becomes Closed after it has been in the Resolved state for a set time and it is confirmed that the issue is satisfactorily resolved. The caller can close it, or a scheduled job can auto-close it after the configured number of days (7 business days by default). See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/incident-management/c_IncidentManagementStateModel.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The incident life cycle lists Resolved and Closed as separate states with different meanings, so they are not two names for one state.
A Resolved incident is not locked. If the caller rejects the resolution, the incident goes back to In Progress and is not auto-closed.
The order is reversed. An incident is Closed after it has been in the Resolved state for a set time, so Closed comes after Resolved.

source.excerpt: Resolved indicates a solution was applied; Closed indicates the caller confirmed the resolution.

questions.question: An administrator wants every new incident in the Network category to go to the Network assignment group automatically, with no scripting. Which feature should they configure?

options.text: A data policy on the Incident table
An assignment rule for the Incident table
An inactivity monitor on the Incident table
A UI policy on the Incident form

explanation.correct: Assignment rules set the Assigned to and Assignment group fields automatically when a record matches a set of conditions. You choose the table, define conditions such as Category is Network, and pick the group in the Assign to section; no script is needed. The product docs use this exact example of Network category incidents. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/t_AssignmentModuleRule.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Data policies enforce data consistency by making fields mandatory or read-only for all data entry. They do not choose an assignment group.
An inactivity monitor fires an event when a task has not been updated for a set time. It reminds people about stale tasks and does not route new ones.
UI policies change form behavior, such as making fields read-only, mandatory or hidden. They do not set an assignment based on the category.

source.excerpt: Assignment Rules automatically assign records to users or groups based on conditions.

questions.question: During a major incident, the network team that owns the incident needs the database team to fail over a cluster. How should the major incident manager request and track this work?

options.text: Create an incident task assigned to the database team
Propose the incident as a major incident candidate
Create a problem record assigned to the database team
Add the database team to a communication plan

explanation.correct: Incident tasks exist so that work can be requested from, and communicated to, assignment groups other than the one initially assigned to the incident. Each task has its own Assignment group, state, priority and work notes, so the database team's failover work is tracked separately while the network team keeps ownership of the major incident. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/incident-management/create-incident-task.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Proposing an incident as a major incident candidate is how a potential major incident is identified. This incident is already a major incident, and proposing it assigns no work.
Problem Management identifies the cause of errors behind related incidents. A problem record is for root cause analysis, not for requesting an urgent recovery action.
Communication plans control who is informed about a major incident and how often. They keep stakeholders updated but do not assign recovery work to a team.

source.excerpt: Major Incident tasks track individual work items during major incident resolution.

questions.question: A service desk lead is training new agents on the incident state model. Which two statements correctly describe an incident state? (Choose two)

options.text: New: the incident is logged but not yet investigated
Closed: set as soon as the agent provides a fix
Canceled: triaged and found to be a duplicate
On Hold: waiting in the queue for an agent to pick up

explanation.correct: In the incident life cycle, New means the incident is logged but not yet investigated. Canceled means the incident was triaged but found to be a duplicate, unnecessary, or not an incident at all. Resolved is the state for a provided fix. Closed follows after the incident has been Resolved for a specific duration and is confirmed. On Hold means responsibility has temporarily shifted to another entity, such as the caller or a vendor. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/incident-management/c_IncidentManagementStateModel.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Providing a fix sets the incident to Resolved, not Closed. An incident is marked Closed only after it has been Resolved for a specific duration and it is confirmed to be satisfactorily resolved.

On Hold does not mean the incident is waiting for an agent. It means responsibility shifts temporarily to another entity (Awaiting Caller, Change, Problem or Vendor) to provide information, evidence or a resolution.

source.excerpt: Default incident states include New, In Progress, On Hold, Resolved, and Closed.

questions.question: A report developer needs a list report that shows incident records only, with no problem or change records mixed in. Which table should the report use as its source?

options.text: Task [task] parent table
Incident [incident] table
Problem [problem] table
Change [change_request] table

explanation.correct: Incident [incident] is the table for incident records. It extends the Task [task] table and inherits Task's standard fields. The platform shows each table in the Task hierarchy as its own logical table, so choosing Incident returns incident records only. Choosing Task would also return problems, changes and other task types. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/c_TaskTable.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Task is the parent table extended by Incident, Problem, Change and others, so a Task report would also include problem and change records.
Problem [problem] is a separate table that extends Task and holds problem records, so it would not return any incidents.
Change [change_request] is a separate Task child table that holds change records, not incidents, so it does not fit the requirement.

source.excerpt: Incident records are stored in the incident table, which extends the task table.

questions.question: A service desk manager wants a report showing which incidents were reopened several times after being resolved. Which Incident form field tracks how many times an incident has been reopened?

options.text: Last reopened by
Reopen count
Last reopened at
Parent Incident

explanation.correct: The Reopen count field on the Incident form tracks how many times an incident has been reopened, which supports reporting on reopened incidents. Last reopened by and Last reopened at record only who reopened the incident most recently and when. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/incident-management/reopening-incident.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Last reopened by is filled with the name of the person who reopened the incident. It records the most recent reopener, not the number of reopens.
Last reopened at is filled with the date and time when the incident was reopened. It is a timestamp, not a count.
Parent Incident holds the number of the incident's parent incident. It relates records and does not track reopens.

source.excerpt: The Reopen count field is incremented when an incident is reopened.

questions.question: An agent logs an incident because a specific mail server has stopped responding. Which Incident form field should the agent use to record the affected server?

options.text: Service offering
Configuration item
Category and Subcategory
Assignment group

explanation.correct: The Configuration item field records the affected CI, such as a specific server. Once it is set, the agent can open the dependency view to see what is impacted and whether other CIs or services have issues. By default, a business rule can also fill in the Assignment group from the CI's support group. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/incident-management/create-an-incident.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Service offering describes the service commitments and level of service for a business service. It does not identify an individual server.
Category and Subcategory describe the type of issue being reported. They do not point to the specific server that is affected.
Assignment group is the group that will work the incident. It can be populated from the CI, but it does not record the affected item.

source.excerpt: The Configuration Item field links incidents to items in the CMDB for impact analysis.

questions.question: An administrator must let a team lead view all incidents and the major incident workbench without being able to update incident records. Which role best fits this need?

options.text: sn_incident_write
sn_incident_read
sn_incident_admin
incident_manager

explanation.correct: The Incident read [sn_incident_read] role gives read access to the Incident Management application and related records. A user with sn_incident_read can view all incidents and the major incident workbench. A user with no role sees only the incidents they created or that were created on their behalf. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/incident-management/inci-roles-instld-itsm-roles.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: sn_incident_write gives write access to the Incident Management application and related records, which is more than the read-only access needed here.
sn_incident_admin configures all Incident Management features, including incident management properties. That is administrative access, not read-only access.
incident_manager manages incident properties and major incident trigger rules and contains the itil / sn_incident_write role, so it allows updates.

source.excerpt: The itil role provides permissions to create, update, and resolve incidents.

questions.question: A service desk manager notices that a P1 incident is still open after its task SLA has run 6 hours in its schedule with no pauses. The SLA definition has a 4-hour duration and a Resolution target. What is true?

options.text: Its Business Elapsed Percentage is still below 100 percent
The task SLA is breached because its breach time has passed
The SLA timer is paused until the caller adds information
The Response target was missed rather than the Resolution one

explanation.correct: An SLA definition's Duration is the time allowed to provide the service, and the task SLA's Breach time is when that time runs out, adjusted for pauses. With 6 hours elapsed against a 4-hour Resolution SLA and no pauses, the breach time has passed while the incident is still open, so the SLA is breached. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/service-level-management/r_TaskSLATable.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Business Elapsed Percentage is the share of the SLA used within the schedule. 6 of 4 hours is 150 percent, well above 100 percent.
The scenario states that no pause time applies. Pauses only happen when the SLA definition's pause conditions are met.
The SLA target set on this task SLA is Resolution, so the breach relates to resolving the incident, not to the first response.

source.excerpt: An SLA breach occurs when an incident exceeds agreed response or resolution times.

questions.question: An administrator wants new incidents to have their Category and Assignment group predicted by machine learning trained on the instance's past incidents, based on each Short description. What should they set up?

options.text: Assignment rules with conditions on the Category field
Predictive Intelligence classification solutions
Priority lookup rules for Impact and Urgency values
A UI policy that makes Category a mandatory field

explanation.correct: Predictive Intelligence for Incident Management uses your instance records to build solutions for Incident Management. Its classification solution definitions include Incident Categorization, which predicts the Category field from the Short description, and Incident Assignment, which predicts the Assignment group field from the Short description. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/predictive-intelligence-for-incident.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Assignment rules set the assigned_to and assignment_group fields when a set of conditions occurs. They are condition-based, do not learn from past records, and do not set the Category.
Priority lookup rules determine how impact and urgency combine into an incident's priority. They do not predict Category or Assignment group.
UI policies change form behavior, for example making a field mandatory or read-only. They do not predict field values from the Short description.

questions.question: An agent working a high-priority incident wants to chat in real time with two network engineers about it, with the conversation tied to the incident record. What should the agent do?

options.text: Add both engineers to the incident's Watch list
Start a Sidebar discussion linked to the incident
Create an incident task for the network group
Add both engineers to the incident's Work notes list

explanation.correct: Sidebar is set up so agents can have real-time collaboration with others. An agent can create a Sidebar discussion for a task record such as an incident, linking it by record number and adding participants who have access to the record. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/conversational-interfaces/sidebar/sidebar-discussions-record.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The Watch list holds users who receive notifications about the incident when comments are added. It sends notifications and does not provide a real-time discussion.
An incident task is used to communicate and request work from assignment groups other than the one assigned to the incident. It is a work record, not a chat.
The Work notes list holds users who receive notifications when work notes are added. It sends notifications and does not provide a real-time discussion.

questions.question: A load balancer stops working, and an agent sets the incident's Configuration item to the server that ran out of memory. Where should the agent record the load balancer and the services that depend on it?

options.text: The Affected CIs related list on the incident
The Watch list field on the incident form
The Parent Incident field on the incident form
The Service Offering field on the incident form

explanation.correct: Use the Configuration item field when a single CI is the cause of the incident. Use the Affected CIs related list when multiple CIs are affected. In the docs example, the Configuration item is the server that is out of memory, and the Affected CIs list contains the load balancer, the data center, dependent servers and impacted business services. From the dependency views map, View Affected CIs and Add Affected CI(s) help find and add them. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/incident-management/t_UsingTheBSMMapToLocateAffectedCIs.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The Watch list holds users who receive notifications when comments are added. It does not record configuration items.
Parent Incident holds the number of the parent incident for this incident. It relates incidents, not affected CIs.
Service Offering identifies a service offering and its service commitments for the incident. It is a single field and does not list the multiple affected CIs.

questions.question: An administrator opens the AI Admin Hub console, where Now Assist generative AI features are set up. Which task is this console designed for?

options.text: Reviewing incident trend reports for the service desk
Installing AI plugins and activating and configuring skills
Creating user groups and assigning roles to the group members
Monitoring CMDB health scores for configuration items

explanation.correct: The AI Admin Hub console gives administrators one place to set up, configure and monitor generative AI applications and features. Its workflow covers installing plugins, optionally turning on the Now Assist panel, activating and configuring skills, reviewing account settings, and monitoring skill performance. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/intelligent-experiences/configuring-now-assist.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Incident status and service level reporting is done with Incident Management dashboards and reports, not with the generative AI admin console.
Groups are created and given roles in User Administration > Groups by a user with the user_admin role, not in the AI admin console.
CMDB health is reviewed in the CMDB Health Dashboard, which shows completeness, correctness and compliance KPIs for CIs.

questions.question: An administrator needs an email sent to the IT Product Owner whenever a Priority 1 incident is created, with the conditions, recipients, and content defined in one record. Which module should they use?

options.text: Routing and Assignment > Assignment Rule
System Notification > Email > Notifications
System Policy > Events > Registry
System Policy > Rules > Priority Lookup Rules

explanation.correct: To create an email notification, navigate to All > System Notification > Email > Notifications and select New. The Notification form has tabs for When to send (conditions), Who will receive (recipients) and What it will contain (contents), so one record defines when, who and what. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/t_CreateANotification.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Assignment rules (All > Routing and Assignment > Assignment Rule) set the assigned_to and assignment_group fields when conditions occur. They do not send email.

The event registry (System Policy > Events > Registry) is where events are registered. Registration lets other parts of the system, such as email notifications and Script Actions, see the event and react to it. The email notification itself is not defined there.
Priority lookup rules (System Policy > Rules > Priority Lookup Rules) define how impact and urgency combine into priority. They do not send notifications.

questions.question: A Tier 2 agent who works incidents, requests, changes, and problems wants one configurable workspace with a landing page showing outages, service announcements, and assignments. Which should they use?

options.text: Service Portal self-service pages
Service Operations Workspace
Service Graph Workspace
Major incident workbench

explanation.correct: Service Operations Workspace for ITSM is a configurable workspace that provides a unified experience for multiple IT Service Management and IT Operations Management workflows. Tier 2 agents (itil role) focus on incidents, requests, changes, problems and major incidents. A tailored landing page gives an overview of outages, service announcements and assignments. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/service-operations-workspace/explore-sow.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Service Portal is used to build a self-service portal experience for employees or customers. It is not an agent workspace for working on ITSM records.
Service Graph Workspace (like CMDB Workspace) is where CMDB Health dashboards, relationship health and CI health are viewed. It is not for working incidents and requests.

The major incident workbench is a single-pane view for managing major incidents, opened from a major incident record. It is not the agent's general workspace for incidents, requests, changes and problems.

questions.question: Twenty users log separate incidents for the same email outage, and the major incident manager has already promoted a major incident for it. How should the twenty user incidents be handled?

options.text: Add them as child incidents of the major incident
Create an incident task on the major incident for each
Close each one now so only the major incident stays open
Place each one On Hold with the reason Awaiting Caller

explanation.correct: Similar incidents are added to a major incident so that the support teams can work on the parent record for a coordinated response process. In the major incident workbench, Find Similar adds the selected incidents, which then appear under the Child Incidents section. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/incident-management/add-similar-inci-mim-workbench.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: An incident task is for communicating and requesting work from assignment groups other than the one assigned to the incident. It does not represent another user's report of the same outage.
An incident is marked Closed only after it has been Resolved for a specific duration and the resolution is confirmed. These incidents are not resolved yet.

On Hold with Awaiting Caller is for when responsibility shifts to the caller to provide more information. These callers have already reported the outage, and the incidents should be linked to the major incident.

questions.question: An administrator wants an incident's resolution SLA to stop adding elapsed time while the incident is On Hold, and to continue counting when work resumes. Which SLA definition condition should they configure?

options.text: Stop condition
Pause condition
Cancel condition
Reset condition

explanation.correct: An SLA definition can have up to six conditions: start, cancel, pause, resume, stop and reset. The pause condition defines when the SLA suspends increasing elapsed time. The When to resume setting (or a resume condition) controls when elapsed time continues to increase. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/service-level-management/c_SLAConditions.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The stop condition defines when the SLA completes. If all stop conditions match, the task SLA completes whether or not it is breached, so it would not continue counting later.
The cancel condition defines the conditions under which the SLA will cancel. It does not suspend and later resume the timer.
The reset condition completes the running SLA and attaches a new one. It does not pause elapsed time on the existing SLA.

questions.question: An administrator has two active assignment rules on the Incident table. Both match a new, unassigned Network incident: Rule A has order 100 and Rule B has order 200. What happens?

options.text: Rule A runs and sets the assignment; Rule B does not run
Both rules run, and Rule B's assignment overwrites Rule A
Neither rule runs because the matching conditions conflict
The most recently created of the two rules is the one that runs

explanation.correct: An assignment rule sets the Assigned to and Assignment group fields automatically when its conditions match a saved, unassigned task. When several rules match, the one with the lowest order value runs and the others do not. Rule A (order 100) assigns the incident, and Rule B (order 200) is skipped. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/c_AssignmentRulesModule.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Assignment rules cannot overwrite an existing assignment, and only the first matching rule by order runs. Rule B never replaces Rule A.
Matching more than one rule is not an error. The rule with the lowest order value runs, so the incident is still assigned.
Precedence comes from the Execution Order value, not the creation date. A lower order value takes priority over a higher one.

questions.question: A caller disagrees with the fix on her Resolved incident and selects the Reopen incident link in the resolution email. What happens to the incident's state?

options.text: It changes from Resolved to In Progress
It changes from Resolved to New
It changes from Resolved to On Hold
It stays Resolved and a new incident opens

explanation.correct: A caller who is not satisfied with a resolution can reopen the incident from the resolution email link or from the Reopen option on the form or portal. Once an incident is reopened, its state changes from Resolved to In Progress. The Last reopened by and Last reopened at fields are filled in at the same time. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/incident-management/reopening-incident.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: A reopened incident does not go back to New, the state for a logged incident that has not been investigated. The docs state that it changes from Resolved to In Progress.
Reopening does not place the incident On Hold. A reopened incident moves from Resolved to In Progress so work can continue.

A new incident is opened only when someone replies to the resolution email for an incident that is already Closed, and that behavior has to be configured. A Resolved incident is reopened and moves to In Progress.

questions.question: An agent logs a new incident with Impact set to 1 - High and Urgency set to 3 - Low. Assuming the standard sample priority lookup rules are in place, which Priority does the incident get?

options.text: 2 - High
3 - Moderate
1 - Critical
4 - Low

explanation.correct: Priority lookup rules determine how impact and urgency values combine into a priority. In the documented sample data lookup rules, Impact 1 - High with Urgency 3 - Low gives Priority 3 - Moderate. A low urgency lowers the priority even when the impact is high. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/incident-management/def-prio-lookup-rules.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: 2 - High is the result for Impact 1 - High with Urgency 2 - Medium (or Impact 2 - Medium with Urgency 1 - High), not for Urgency 3 - Low.
1 - Critical needs both Impact 1 - High and Urgency 1 - High in the sample priority lookup rules.
4 - Low comes from a Low impact combined with Medium or Low urgency (or Medium impact with Low urgency). It does not come from a High impact.

questions.question: A user phones the service desk about a broken laptop, and the agent logs an incident during the call. Which Incident form field identifies the user who reported the issue?

options.text: Caller
Assigned to
Channel
Watch list

explanation.correct: On the Incident form, the Caller field is the user who contacted you with an issue. In this scenario, that is the employee who phoned about the laptop. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/incident-management/create-an-incident.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Assigned to is the user who works on the incident, not the user who reported it.
Channel records the communication method used to create the incident (for example Phone or Email), not which user reported it.
The Watch list holds users who receive notifications when comments are added. It does not identify the reporting user.
